claim: Mutations in the human BEST1 gene lead to retinal degenerative diseases displaying progressive vision loss and even blindness.
source: Mutations in the human BEST1 gene lead to retinal degenerative diseases displaying progressive vision loss and even blindness.
evidence: This is a general statement about BEST1 mutations and their clinical consequences, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: BESTROPHIN1, encoded by BEST1, is predominantly expressed in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE).
source: BESTROPHIN1, encoded by BEST1, is predominantly expressed in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), but its physiological role has been a mystery for the last two decades.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies in the introduction.

claim: The disease-causing mechanism of BEST1 mutations is centered on the indispensable role of BESTROPHIN1 in mediating Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in RPE.
source: Our results revealed that the disease-causing mechanism of BEST1 mutations is centered on the indispensable role of BESTROPHIN1 in mediating the long speculated Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in RPE
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data from iPSC-RPE and other systems.

claim: Patient RPE is rescuable with viral gene supplementation.
source: Moreover, we demonstrated that patient RPE is rescuable with viral gene supplementation, providing a proof-of-concept for curing BEST1-associated diseases.
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in the study with BacMam viral vectors expressing WT BEST1.

claim: Over 200 distinct mutations in BEST1 have been identified to associate with bestrophinopathies.
source: To date, over 200 distinct mutations in BEST1 have been identified to associate with bestrophinopathies (http://www-huge.uni-regensburg.de/BEST1_database/home.php?select_db=BEST1)
evidence: This is supported by reference to a database of BEST1 mutations.

claim: Bestrophinopathies consist of at least five distinct retinal degeneration disorders.
source: which consist of at least five distinct retinal degeneration disorders, namely: Best vitelliform macular dystrophy (BVMD) (Marquardt et al., 1998; Petrukhin et al., 1998), autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy (ARB) (Burgess et al., 2008), adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy (AVMD) (Allikmets et al., 1999; Krämer et al., 2000), autosomal dominant vitreoretinochoroidopathy (ADVIRC) (Yardley et al., 2004), and retinitis pigmentosa (RP) (Davidson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies identifying these disorders.

claim: Patients with bestrophinopathies are susceptible to progressive vision loss for which there is currently no treatment available.
source: Patients with bestrophinopathies are susceptible to progressive vision loss for which there is currently no treatment available.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical prognosis and current treatment options, based on established knowledge.

claim: A clinical feature of bestrophinopathies associated with BEST1 mutations is abnormal electrooculogram (EOG) light peak (LP).
source: A clinical feature of bestrophinopathies associated with BEST1 mutations is abnormal electrooculogram (EOG) light peak (LP), measured by the maximum transepithelial potential produced by RPE upon light exposure (Boon et al., 2009; Marmorstein et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous clinical studies.

claim: LP is believed to represent a depolarization of the basolateral membrane of RPE due to activation of a Cl- conductance triggered by changes in intracellular Ca2+ concentration.
source: LP is believed to represent a depolarization of the basolateral membrane of RPE due to activation of a Cl- conductance triggered by changes in intracellular Ca2+ concentration ([Ca2+]i) (Fujii et al., 1992; Gallemore and Steinberg, 1989; Gallemore and Steinberg, 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous physiological studies.

claim: The existence of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current on the plasma membrane of RPE has not yet been directly demonstrated.
source: However, the existence of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current on the plasma membrane of RPE has not yet been directly demonstrated, let alone the identity of the participating channel(s).
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: BEST1 localizes to the basolateral membrane of RPE.
source: BEST1 localizes to the basolateral membrane of RPE (Marmorstein et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: BEST1 has been functionally identified as a CaCC in heterologous expression studies.
source: and has been functionally identified as a CaCC in heterologous expression studies (Hartzell et al., 2008; Kane Dickson et al., 2014; Sun et al., 2002; Tsunenari et al., 2003; Xiao et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous functional studies.

claim: Best1 knock-out mice do not have any retinal phenotype or Cl- current abnormality.
source: Best1 knock-out mice do not have any retinal phenotype or Cl- current abnormality (Marmorstein et al., 2006; Milenkovic et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous mouse studies.

claim: There are fundamental differences between humans and mice regarding the genetic bases for electrophysiological responses in RPE.
source: suggesting that either BEST1 is not the Cl- conducting channel in RPE, or that there are fundamental differences between humans and mice regarding the genetic bases for this electrophysiological response.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mouse knockouts don't show phenotypes while human mutations do.

claim: BEST1 localized on the plasma membrane of iPSC-RPE.
source: We found that BEST1 localized on the plasma membrane of iPSC-RPE (Figure 1A, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images showing co-localization with plasma membrane markers.

claim: Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents were recorded on the plasma membrane of iPSC-RPE with currents being tiny (< 5 pA/pF) when [Ca2+]i was 0.
source: Currents were tiny (< 5 pA/pF) when [Ca2+]i was 0 (Figure 1B,C)
evidence: This is directly measured by whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents increased in amplitude as [Ca2+]i was raised from 100 nM to 4.2 μM, peaking at 358 ± 15 pA/pF at 1.2 and 4.2 μM [Ca2+]i.
source: and increased in amplitude as [Ca2+]i was raised from 100 nM to 4.2 μM, peaking at 358 ± 15 pA/pF at 1.2 and 4.2 μM [Ca2+]i (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is directly measured by whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: The measured currents in iPSC-RPE were inhibited by the Cl- channel blocker niflumic acid (NFA).
source: The measured currents were inhibited by the Cl- channel blocker niflumic acid (NFA) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), demonstrating that these were indeed Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents.
evidence: This is demonstrated by pharmacological inhibition experiments.

claim: The half maximal effective concentration (EC50) of Ca2+ for Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in iPSC-RPE is 455 nM.
source: A plot of peak current (evoked with a +100 mV step pulse) as a function of [Ca2+]i displayed robust Ca2+-dependent activation with the half maximal effective concentration (EC50) of Ca2+ at 455 nM.
evidence: This is calculated from dose-response data obtained by patch clamp.

claim: Similar Ca2+-dependent Cl- current profiles were recorded in iPSC-RPEs derived from two independent BEST1 WT donors.
source: Similar Ca2+-dependent Cl- current profiles were recorded in iPSC-RPEs derived from two independent BEST1 WT donors, and in iPSC-RPEs from two distinct clonal iPSCs of the same donor (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing data from multiple independent donors.

claim: BEST1 was plasma membrane enriched in fetal human RPE (fhRPE).
source: Consistent with the results from iPSC-RPEs, BEST1 was plasma membrane enriched (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images.

claim: A similar pattern of Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents was recorded in fhRPEs from two independent fetuses.
source: and a similar pattern of Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents was recorded in fhRPEs from two independent fetuses (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: The Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in fhRPEs displayed a lower Ca2+ sensitivity compared to that in iPSC-RPEs (EC50 1.7 μM vs. 455 nM).
source: Interestingly, despite their comparable initial and peak amplitudes, the Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in fhRPEs displayed a lower Ca2+ sensitivity compared to that in iPSC-RPEs (EC50 1.7 μM vs. 455 nM, Figure 2D)
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing dose-response curves from patch clamp experiments.

claim: The difference in Ca2+ sensitivity between fhRPE and iPSC-RPE may reflect the different requirement of LP generation in RPE during different developmental stages.
source: which may reflect the different requirement of LP generation in RPE during different developmental stages.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed difference in Ca2+ sensitivity.

claim: The subcellular localization of BEST1 and the properties of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in iPSC-RPE resemble those in fhRPE.
source: Overall, the subcellular localization of BEST1 and the properties of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in iPSC-RPE resemble those in fhRPE, validating iPSC-RPE as a powerful platform to study the influence of BEST1 mutations on RPE surface Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of data from iPSC-RPE and fhRPE.

claim: When the pipet solution contained high (18 μM) [Ca2+]i, the currents in fhRPE ran up after patch break with a half-time of ~2.5 min and reached a plateau that was on average 7.8-fold greater than the initial current.
source: It is worth to note that during patch clamp recording with fhRPE, when the pipet solution contained high (18 μM) [Ca2+]i, the currents ran up after patch break with a half-time of ~2.5 min and reached a plateau that was on average 7.8-fold greater than the initial current (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is observed in time-course experiments during patch clamp recordings.

claim: When the pipet solution contained low (0.6 μM) [Ca2+]i, the currents in fhRPE remained stable after patch break.
source: In contrast, when the pipet solution contained low (0.6 μM) [Ca2+]i, the currents remained stable after patch break (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is observed in time-course experiments during patch clamp recordings.

claim: ARB is associated with recessive mutations in BEST1.
source: Unlike the other bestrophinopathies caused by autosomal dominant mutations in BEST1, ARB is associated with recessive mutations.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic basis of ARB.

claim: Patients with ARB are characterized by progressive generalized rod-cone degenerations, typically with a visual acuity reading around 20/40 in the first decade of life.
source: Patients with ARB are characterized by progressive generalized rod-cone degenerations, typically with a visual acuity reading around 20/40 in the first decade of life, and their vision progressively worsens over time (Burgess et al., 2008; Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous clinical studies.

claim: Both ARB patients exhibit typical ARB phenotypes in fundus autofluorescence imaging, spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SDOCT) and full-field electroretinography (ERG).
source: Both patients exhibit typical ARB phenotypes in fundus autofluorescence imaging, spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SDOCT) and full-field electroretinography (ERG) (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by clinical imaging and electrophysiology data from the patients.

claim: Patient 1 has a homozygous c.821C > G; p.P274R mutation in BEST1.
source: Patient 1, a 12-year-old otherwise healthy boy, who has a previously described homozygous c.821C > G; p.P274R mutation in BEST1 (Fung et al., 2015; Kinnick et al., 2011)
evidence: This is confirmed by genetic sequencing and supported by previous reports.

claim: Patient 1 showed reduced visual acuities at 20/60 and 20/70 in the right and left eye, respectively.
source: showed reduced visual acuities at 20/60 and 20/70 in the right and left eye, respectively.
evidence: This is clinical data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 1's color fundus showed bilateral, confluent curvilinear subretinal yellowish vitelliform deposits to the optic disks.
source: Color fundus showed bilateral, confluent curvilinear subretinal yellowish vitelliform deposits to the optic disks, which over 3 years of follow-up became more multifocal and dispersed to involve the nasal retinae (Figure 3A, left).
evidence: This is clinical imaging data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 1's SDOCT discovered bilateral, multifocal serous retinal detachments involving the maculae and cystoid changes in the macula.
source: SDOCT discovered bilateral, multifocal serous retinal detachments involving the maculae and cystoid changes in the macula (Figure 3B, left).
evidence: This is clinical imaging data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 1's maximum response of ERG b-wave were 132.6 μV and 194.4 μV in the right and left eye, respectively, contrasting 355 μV (median value) in healthy teenagers.
source: Maximum response of ERG b-wave (amplitudes between a- and b-wave) were 132.6 μV and 194.4 μV in the right and left eye, respectively, contrasting 355 μV (median value) in healthy teenagers tested in the same device (Figure 3C, left).
evidence: This is clinical electrophysiology data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 2 has a homozygous c.602T > C; p.I201T mutation in BEST1.
source: Patient 2, a 72-year-old otherwise healthy man, who has a homozygous c.602T > C; p.I201T mutation in BEST1
evidence: This is confirmed by genetic sequencing.

claim: Patient 2 showed a dropped vision acuity at 20/40 in the right eye, and 20/200 in the left eye mainly due to aging-caused retinal atrophy.
source: showed a dropped vision acuity at 20/40 in the right eye, and 20/200 in the left eye mainly due to aging-caused retinal atrophy.
evidence: This is clinical data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 2's color fundus presented less vitelliform deposits compared with patient 1.
source: His color fundus presented less vitelliform deposits compared with patient 1, and aging-caused dispersed punctate fleck lesions in the left eye (Figure 3A, right).
evidence: This is clinical imaging data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 2's SDOCT showed milder cystic degeneration compared to that in Patient 1.
source: SDOCT showed milder cystic degeneration compared to that in Patient 1 (Figure 3B, right).
evidence: This is clinical imaging data from patient examination.

claim: Patient 2's maximum responses of ERG b-waves were 103.2 μV and 79.6 μV in the right and left eye, respectively, contrasting 287 μV (median value) in age-matched healthy people.
source: Maximum responses of ERG b-waves were 103.2 μV and 79.6 μV in the right and left eye, respectively, contrasting 287 μV (median value) in age-matched healthy people (Figure 3C, right).
evidence: This is clinical electrophysiology data from patient examination.

claim: The I201T mutation is less severe than the P274R mutation.
source: In summary, even though ARB has progressed for 60 years longer, patient 2 has better vision acuity (in his more relevant right eye), less vitelliform deposit, milder cystic degeneration, and better responses to visual stimuli, suggesting that the I201T mutation is less severe than the P274R mutation.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the clinical phenotypes of the two patients.

claim: RPE-specific marker proteins RPE65 and CRALBP displayed similar expression levels in the BEST1 WT and two patient-derived iPSC-RPEs.
source: RPE-specific marker proteins RPE65 (retinal pigment epithelium-specific 65 kDa protein) and CRALBP (cellular retinaldehyde-binding protein) displayed similar expression levels in the BEST1 WT and two patient-derived iPSC-RPEs by western blot (Figure 4A), confirming the mature status of iPSC-RPEs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis.

claim: Patient iPSC-RPE carrying the BEST1 P274R mutation showed a similar overall BEST1 expression level compared to that in WT iPSC-RPE.
source: Patient iPSC-RPE carrying the BEST1 P274R mutation showed a similar overall BEST1 expression level compared to that in WT iPSC-RPE (Figure 4A) in western blot
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis.

claim: P274R patient iPSC-RPE exhibited diminished BEST1 antibody staining on the plasma membrane.
source: but exhibited diminished BEST1 antibody staining on the plasma membrane (Figure 4B, top), indicating that the subcellular localization of the channel was severely impaired by the P274R mutation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy.

claim: Tiny currents (< 6 pA/pF) were detected in P274R patient iPSC-RPE at all tested [Ca2+]i.
source: Strikingly, tiny currents (< 6 pA/pF) were detected in P274R patient iPSC-RPE at all tested [Ca2+]i by whole-cell patch clamp (Figure 4C-E p, and Figure 1—source data 1), indicating that the P274R mutation abolishes Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in RPE.
evidence: This is demonstrated by whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: Both the membrane localization of BEST1 and the Ca2+-dependent Cl- current were rescued in P274R patient iPSC-RPE by complementation with WT BEST1-GFP expressed from a BacMam baculoviral vector.
source: Furthermore, both the membrane localization of BEST1 and the Ca2+-dependent Cl- current were rescued in P274R patient iPSC-RPE by complementation with WT BEST1-GFP expressed from a BacMam baculoviral vector (Figure 4E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B,C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and patch clamp experiments.

claim: Functional BEST1 is necessary for generating Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in human RPE.
source: These results demonstrated that functional BEST1 is necessary for generating Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in human RPE.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that WT BEST1 restores currents in P274R mutant cells.

claim: Patient iPSC-RPE carrying the BEST1 I201T mutation showed a similar overall BEST1 level compared to that in WT iPSC-RPE.
source: On the other hand, patient iPSC-RPE carrying the BEST1 I201T mutation showed a similar overall BEST1 level compared to that in WT iPSC-RPE (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis.

claim: I201T patient iPSC-RPE showed normal BEST1 antibody staining on the plasma membrane.
source: and normal BEST1 antibody staining on the plasma membrane (Figure 4B, bottom).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy.

claim: I201T patient iPSC-RPE displayed robust but significantly decreased Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents compared to those in WT iPSC-RPE.
source: However, I201T patient iPSC-RPE displayed robust but significantly decreased Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents compared to those in WT iPSC-RPE (Figure 4C,D,F, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: The pattern of Ca2+ response was similar in WT and I201T iPSC-RPEs (EC50 455 nM vs. 526 nM) when current amplitudes were normalized.
source: Notably, when current amplitudes were normalized, the pattern of Ca2+ response was similar in WT and I201T iPSC-RPEs (EC50 455 nM vs. 526 nM, Figure 4F, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), indicating that the Ca2+ sensitivity of surface Cl- current in RPE is not altered by the I201T mutation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing normalized dose-response curves from patch clamp experiments.

claim: The P274R mutation leads to a 'null' phenotype of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in RPE associated with a loss of BEST1 plasma membrane enrichment.
source: Taken together, our results showed that the P274R mutation leads to a 'null' phenotype of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in RPE associated with a loss of BEST1 plasma membrane enrichment
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from iPSC-RPE studies.

claim: The I201T mutation causes reduced Cl- current in RPE without altering Ca2+ sensitivity of the current or subcellular localization of BEST1.
source: while the seemingly milder I201T mutation causes reduced Cl- current in RPE without altering Ca2+ sensitivity of the current or subcellular localization of BEST1.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from iPSC-RPE studies.

claim: There is a strong correlation between the status of BEST1, the functionality of RPE surface Ca2+-dependent Cl- current, and retinal physiology.
source: Importantly, the P274R patient exhibits a more severe retinal phenotype compared to the I201T patient, suggesting a strong correlation between the status of BEST1, the functionality of RPE surface Ca2+-dependent Cl- current, and retinal physiology.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the clinical phenotypes with the functional data.

claim: HEK293 cells do not have any endogenous CaCC on the plasma membrane.
source: To directly examine the influence of the disease-causing mutations on BEST1, WT and mutant BEST1 channels were individually introduced into HEK293 cells, which do not have any endogenous CaCC on the plasma membrane (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch clamp experiments on untransfected HEK293 cells.

claim: Both WT and the mutant BEST1 channels were expressed at similar levels after transient transfection in HEK293 cells.
source: Western blot confirmed that both WT and the mutant channels were expressed at similar levels after transient transfection (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis.

claim: HEK293 cells expressing WT BEST1 displayed robust Ca2+-dependent currents markedly inhibited by NFA.
source: As previously reported, HEK293 cells expressing WT BEST1 displayed robust Ca2+-dependent currents markedly inhibited by NFA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), indicating that they were Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents (Hartzell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch clamp experiments with pharmacological inhibition.

claim: HEK293 cells expressing the P274R mutant yielded no current.
source: Consistent with the results in iPSC-RPE, HEK293 cells expressing the P274R mutant yielded no current
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch clamp experiments.

claim: HEK293 cells expressing the I201T mutant displayed significantly smaller current amplitude compared to that of WT at 1.2 μM [Ca2+]i.
source: while cells expressing the I201T mutant displayed significantly smaller current amplitude compared to that of WT at 1.2 μM [Ca2+]i, where HEK293 cells expressing WT BEST1 conduct peak current amplitude (Figure 5A,B) (Hartzell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch clamp experiments.

claim: The two disease-causing mutations lead to distinct defects of the BEST1 channel activity that match the defects of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in iPSC-RPEs.
source: As HEK293 cells represent a 'blank' background, the recorded Ca2+-dependent Cl- currents are genuinely generated from transiently transfected BEST1 channels. Therefore, the two disease-causing mutations lead to distinct defects of the BEST1 channel activity that match the defects of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in iPSC-RPEs
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the results in HEK293 cells with those in iPSC-RPE.

claim: BEST1 is the bona fide CaCC on the plasma membrane of RPE mediating Ca2+-dependent Cl- current for LP.
source: strongly suggesting that BEST1 is the bona fide CaCC on the plasma membrane of RPE mediating Ca2+-dependent Cl- current for LP.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results in iPSC-RPE and HEK293 cells.

claim: BEST1 P274 is identical in KpBest (P239) based on sequence alignment.
source: Sequence alignment reveals that BEST1 P274 is identical while I201 has a highly conservative substitution in KpBest (P239 and L177, respectively, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment analysis.

claim: BEST1 I201 has a highly conservative substitution in KpBest (L177).
source: Sequence alignment reveals that BEST1 P274 is identical while I201 has a highly conservative substitution in KpBest (P239 and L177, respectively, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The yield of pentameric KpBest P239R was significantly less compared to that of KpBest WT or L177T during protein purification.
source: During protein purification, we noticed that the yield of pentameric KpBest P239R was significantly less compared to that of KpBest WT or L177T (Figure 7A), consistent with the prediction that P274R causes massive disruption, and thus instability, to the channel structure.
evidence: This is demonstrated by protein purification experiments.

claim: No crystal was grown with KpBest P239R.
source: While no crystal was grown with KpBest P239R
evidence: This is an observation from crystallization experiments.

claim: Well-diffracted KpBest L177T crystals were obtained under the same condition as KpBest WT.
source: well-diffracted KpBest L177T crystals were obtained under the same condition as KpBest WT (Yang et al., 2014b), and the structure was solved to 3.1 Å resolution (Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by crystallization and X-ray diffraction experiments.

claim: The KpBest L177T structure mirrors that of KpBest WT, with all-atom alignment RMSD in a protomer 0.4 Å.
source: The KpBest L177T structure mirrors that of KpBest WT, with all-atom alignment RMSD (root-mean-square deviation) in a protomer 0.4 Å (Coot LSQ superpose).
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural analysis of the crystal structure.

claim: Superposition of KpBest WT with the L177T mutant based on the alignment of single chain residues 174–180 showed an obvious shift of the TM region.
source: However, superposition of KpBest WT with the L177T mutant based on the alignment of single chain residues 174–180 showed an obvious shift of the TM region (Figure 8, and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural analysis of the crystal structure.

claim: Single channel currents were recorded with KpBest WT at 80 mV with mean amplitude of 5.5 pA.
source: As previously described (Yang et al., 2014b), purified KpBest channels were fused into planar lipid bilayer with 150 mM NaCl in both the trans (internal) and cis (external) solutions, and single channel currents were recorded with KpBest WT at 80 mV with mean amplitude of 5.5 pA (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single channel recordings in lipid bilayers.

claim: No currents were obtained with KpBest P239R in lipid bilayer recordings.
source: By contrast, no currents were obtained with KpBest P239R
evidence: This is demonstrated by single channel recordings in lipid bilayers.

claim: Currents with reduced unitary conductance (mean amplitude 1.5 pA) were recorded with KpBest L177T.
source: while currents with reduced unitary conductance (mean amplitude 1.5 pA) were recorded with KpBest L177T (Figure 7B,C)
evidence: This is demonstrated by single channel recordings in lipid bilayers.

claim: The BEST1 P274R and I201T mutations result in a complete and partial loss of single channel activity, respectively.
source: suggesting that the BEST1 P274R and I201T mutations result in a complete and partial loss of single channel activity, respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from the single channel recordings with KpBest mutants.

claim: P274R is a null mutation that abolishes both plasma membrane localization and channel activity of BEST1 due to structural disruption.
source: Taken together, we concluded that P274R is a null mutation that abolishes both plasma membrane localization and channel activity of BEST1 due to structural disruption
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined structural and functional data.

claim: I201T is a partial loss-of-function mutation that retains plasma membrane localization and Ca2+ sensitivity of BEST1 caused by minor structural alterations.
source: whereas I201T is a partial loss-of-function mutation that retains plasma membrane localization and Ca2+ sensitivity of BEST1 caused by minor structural alterations.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined structural and functional data.

claim: P274 locates at the N-terminal of helix S4a in the BEST1 homology model.
source: In this BEST1 model, P274 locates at the N-terminal of helix S4a (Figure 6A,B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on the human BEST1 homology model.

claim: The presence of Pro in alpha helices normally promotes thermostability of the membrane protein.
source: The presence of Pro in alpha helices normally promotes thermostability of the membrane protein (Reiersen and Rees, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Substitution of Pro with Arg will release the restrictions and induce instability of local structure.
source: Substitution of Pro with Arg will release the restrictions and induce instability of local structure, predicting a dramatic disruption of the channel.
evidence: This is inferred from structural principles and the homology model.

claim: I201 resides in a loop between S2h and S3a in the BEST1 homology model.
source: On the other hand, I201 resides in a loop between S2h and S3a (Figure 6A,B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is based on the human BEST1 homology model.

claim: I201 is surrounded by hydrophobic residues V114, A195, L207, and L210, which are conserved among species.
source: surrounded by hydrophobic residues V114, A195, L207, and L210 (Figure 6C), which are conserved among species and thus probably important for the channel function (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on the homology model and sequence alignment.

claim: The Ile to Thr substitution changes a hydrophobic residue to a polar residue, which weakens the hydrophobic interactions.
source: As the Ile to Thr substitution changes a hydrophobic residue to a polar residue, which weakens the hydrophobic interactions, this mutation may change the channel property by altering the local interplays between spatially adjacent subunits
evidence: This is inferred from structural principles and the homology model.

claim: I205 is a putative activation/permeation gate and the narrowest exit along the ion conducting pathway.
source: Importantly, the potential influence of the I201T mutation on the channel function is underlined by its proximity to I205 (Figure 6A,C), a putative activation/permeation gate and the narrowest exit along the ion conducting pathway (Figure 6A,B) (Yang et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous structural study.

claim: Best1 knockout mice do not have any retinal abnormality or aberrant Cl- current, unlike the phenotypes seen with human BEST1 mutations.
source: It should be noted that Best1 knockout mice do not have any retinal abnormality or aberrant Cl- current (Marmorstein et al., 2006; Milenkovic et al., 2015), unlike the phenotypes seen with human BEST1 mutations, suggesting different genetic requirements for retinal physiology among species.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous mouse studies and inferred from the comparison.

claim: The Ca2+ sensitivity observed in BEST1 WT iPSC-RPE (EC50 455 nM) is at levels more comparable to physiological conditions than that detected in HEK293 cells over-expressing BEST1 (EC50 ~150 nM).
source: Notably, the Ca2+ sensitivity observed in BEST1 WT iPSC-RPE (EC50 455 nM) is at levels more comparable to physiological conditions than that detected in HEK293 cells over-expressing BEST1 (EC50 ~150 nM), let alone cBest1 in bilayer (EC50 17 nM), because basal [Ca2+]i in the human body is typically around 100 nM
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the EC50 values with physiological Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: The loss of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in the 'null' BEST1 P274R iPSC-RPE was rescued by viral expression of WT BEST1.
source: In regard to the clinical treatment of bestrophinopathies, our study provided an important proof-of-concept for treating ARB caused by BEST1 recessive mutations, as the loss of Ca2+-dependent Cl- current in the 'null' BEST1 P274R iPSC-RPE was rescued by viral expression of WT BEST1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the complementation experiments.

claim: Most of the BEST1 patient-specific mutations are dominant.
source: Notably, most of the BEST1 patient-specific mutations are dominant
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about bestrophinopathies.

source: On the other hand, recessive BEST1 mutations from ARB patients provide a unique opportunity to analyze and connect the structure, function and physiological role of BEST1 in a 'clean' manner, as only the mutant BEST1 proteins are present in patients and all our experimental systems.
